dedupe_keys.name: cedar madrigal upper atmospheric science database

description: Madrigal is a web-based system for managing and serving archival and real-time data from a wide range of upper atmospheric science instruments, used by research groups around the world; the CEDAR Madrigal site serves the Coupling, Energetics and Dynamics of Atmospheric Regions (CEDAR) programme, and Madrigal sites share metadata. It holds upper atmosphere observations organised as experiments, which users can browse, download in several formats, combine through a derivation engine or access through APIs for MATLAB, Python and IDL. It covers instruments worldwide, with each Madrigal site controlling and updating its own data. The database is maintained by William Rideout and Katherine Cariglia, who ask users to cite the CEDAR Madrigal Database, and states that its architecture meets FAIR principles. Access is free and needs no prior permission, but use is subject to the CEDAR Rules of the Road, which require early contact with the organisations whose data are used. Caveats: instrument files differ in parameters and quality flags, and some data carry limitations that are not evident to new users. It supports hazard exposure studies of space weather effects on radio, GNSS and satellite systems and validation of ionosphere models; a related record is the NASA CDAWeb space physics data service.
